content: 1. Drain lines for equipment, including condensate drain lines from refrigeration units, must be designed to minimize the distance between the drain line outlet and the deck scupper drain. 2. Whenever feasible, drain lines should run in a straight vertical line to the deck scupper drain. 3. If a straight vertical line is not possible, the horizontal distance of the drain line should be kept as short as possible. 4. The outlet of the drain line must terminate at least 2 cm above the deck. 5. Electrical enclosures located in catering spaces must comply with the International Electrical Code. 6. Electrical wiring from permanently installed equipment must be encased in stainless steel. 7. Ozone or ultraviolet equipment must not be installed in provisions rooms or food preparation areas unless the equipment is constructed of non-corroding stainless steel with fasteners that meet the requirements outlined in Section VI. 8. Bulkhead-mounted equipment installations, such as phones, speakers, and cameras, must be sealed tightly with the bulkhead panels and should not be placed in areas exposed to moisture, food splashes, or grease. 9. All areas where electrical lines, steam, or water pipelines penetrate the panels or tiles of the deck, bulkhead, or deckhead must be tightly sealed. Openings between the electrical lines or pipelines and the surrounding conduit or pipelines must also be sealed. 10. Steam and water pipelines leading to kettles and boilers must be encased in stainless steel cabinets or positioned behind bulkhead panels. A minimal amount of exposed pipeline is acceptable. 11. Hood systems or direct duct exhaust must be installed over ware washing equipment, including three-compartment sinks in pot wash areas (this does not apply to under-counter dishwashing machines). 12. For ware washing machines with direct duct exhaust, the exhaust must be directly connected to the hood exhaust trunk. 13. Exhaust hoods over ware washing equipment or three-compartment sinks must have a minimum six-inch overhang from the edge of the equipment to capture excess steam and vapors. 14. Ware washing machines with direct duct exhaust to the ventilation system must have a clean-out port in each duct, located between the top of the ware washing machine and the hood system or deckhead. 15. Flat condensate drip pans located in the ducts from ware washing machines must be removable for cleaning. 16. Hood systems must be installed above cooking equipment to ensure the removal of excess steam and grease-laden vapors. 17. For bains-marie or steam tables, excess heat and steam must be controlled using either hood systems or dedicated local ventilation extraction. 18. Exhaust vents must be appropriately sized and located to capture heat and steam effectively. 19. Filters, where used, must be easily removable. 20. Vents and ductwork must be accessible for cleaning. Hood washing systems are recommended for removing grease generated from cooking equipment. 21. Continuous welds or profile strips must be used on adjoining pieces of stainless steel, with a minimum 5 mm radius. 22. Drainage systems are not required for manually applied cleaning solutions or grease from hood assemblies. However, drainage systems are required for hood assemblies utilizing automatic wash-down systems. 23. Ventilation systems must comply with manufacturers' recommendations. 24. Walk-in refrigerators and freezers must be constructed with stainless steel panels (minimum thickness of 0.8 mm). Stainless steel panels are preferred for dry storage areas, while painted steel may be used for provisions passageways and dry stores areas. 25. Stainless steel deck panels, such as diamond plate panels, must be used in provisions rooms. All bulkheads and deck junctions must be coved and sealed tightly. 26. If forklifts are used in provisions rooms, the stainless steel panels must be reinforced to prevent buckling. Corrugated stainless steel panels or painted steel must be used in all provisions passageways. 27. Evaporators in walk-in refrigerators, freezers, and dry stores must be constructed with stainless steel panels that cover piping, wiring, coils, and other components that are difficult to clean.
